common_name: Everdi Carex (EverColor Dwarf Glossy Green Sedge)

planting.note: Set divisions or container plants into moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in spring; Everdi is a compact, solid-glossy-green sport of 'Evergold' in the EverColor series and keeps a tighter, denser mound than its variegated relatives.

directions: Grow in evenly moist, fertile, well-drained soil in part shade, where the glossy dark-green, fine-textured blades form a dense, rounded dwarf mound noticeably neater and more compact than other EverColor sedges. Because Everdi lacks variegation, it holds its deep color reliably without the bleaching risk that pale-edged siblings face in brighter spots, though hot afternoon sun can still scorch the leaf tips. Use it as a tidy edger, small-scale groundcover, or container filler where a refined, uniform dark-green texture is wanted. Trim away any winter-damaged foliage in late winter to refresh the clump before spring growth resumes.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in moist, well-drained soil in spring; Everlite is the smallest-growing cultivar in the EverColor series, forming a dense tuft well suited to pots and tight edging spots.

directions: Site in part shade with consistently moist, fertile soil, where the narrow arching leaves display a creamy-white center edged in dark green, giving a bright but fine-grained variegation. Its diminutive, clumping habit makes it one of the most compact sedges for mixed containers, border edging, and small-space groundcover, staying tidy without the spreading tendency of some sedge relatives. Light is a balancing act: enough sun keeps the cream coloring crisp, but intense afternoon exposure can scorch the pale leaf centers, so morning sun with afternoon shade is ideal in hot climates. Shear back tattered foliage in late winter to encourage fresh, brightly variegated growth each spring.
